aiGuidance.extraction: Title: give every problem a title, a short noun phrase of about 3 to 8 words naming the problem's core, so a human scanning a list or outline can tell it from its neighbours. Derive it from the record's own statement. Distinct from sibling titles. Examples of the style: "Training data omits unwritten knowledge", "Decisions lost between meetings". The problem id is a code, not a title; the title does not replace it.
aiGuidance.negativeGuidance: Title must not be the problem id, a truncated or reworded-in-full statement, its first words, or a generic phrase such as "A problem about decisions". It must not strengthen or soften what the statement says. Never overwrite a title a person has set.
aiGuidance.purpose: One problem statement extracted from the source material — a claim with its citation id and classifying facets.

description: A single problem statement: a claim, tagged by kind, persona, scale, context and size.
